data.name: Giles Work Summary Daily Activity Report - 7.7.226
data.notes:
Executive Summary – Daily Activity Report

Today’s focus was split across operational support, procurement, automation development, IT troubleshooting, and project/process improvements.

Key Achievements

Hermes Pipeline Recovery & Development Governance
    Investigated and resolved a failure within the Hermes pipeline after a project rename caused processing issues.
    Restarted and reconfigured the bot, completed root cause analysis, and documented corrective actions.
    Identified wider concerns around Hermes/OpenClaw project mirroring and database structure.
    Initiated a full review of the development workflow and established a new centralised Asana project, aligning management practices with existing successful project structures.
    Connected automation bots to the new Asana project to improve visibility, tracking, and management of development work and fixes.
Procurement & Supply Chain Management
    Processed and reviewed outstanding purchase orders and deliveries.
    Chased overdue supplier deliveries and addressed supplier cancellations.
    Managed credit control matters relating to incoming payments.
    Progressed Keyence orders and reviewed tape switch quotations for the traversing lift project.
    Assessed whether to replace tape switch assemblies completely or refurbish existing units.
    Processed fan orders and coordinated galvanizing requirements, including additional documentation and shipment verification.
Production & Manufacturing Support
    Prepared and issued plating documentation for galvanizing and Broadway Brass.
    Completed a separate 10-page plating report required for ongoing gold finishing work.
    Investigated the Brook Theatre project and identified that the design had progressed to powder coating while legacy BOMs remained open, requiring corrective action.
    Processed documentation and technical information relating to the Hennig repair RFQ, including image preparation, drawing updates, and supplier communication.
Automation & Systems Improvements
    Advanced Asana automation by developing and implementing autotagging workflows and project completion tracking.
    Supported project administration activities, including updates linked to the Cambridge Lift project.
    Investigated and resolved issues within the holiday request cancellation workflow, identifying an edge-case failure requiring correction.
Data Extraction & Recruitment Processing
    Responded to an urgent request to extract CV data from a government portal.
    After authentication issues with Gumloop, developed a local extraction process using browser-based scraping.
    Extracted hyperlinks and source URLs, implemented a Chromium Bridge integration, converted results into structured JSON, separated documents into PDFs, and processed 72 candidate CVs against the relevant job description.
    Imported processed candidate information into Asana for further review.
IT Infrastructure & Remote Working
    Investigated remote access failures affecting home working capability.
    Identified compatibility issues between Tailscale and TeamViewer.
    Conducted alternative Remote Desktop trials and troubleshooting, although some connectivity challenges remain unresolved.
    Resolved a credit card access issue triggered by failed tile authentication.

Overall Outcome

The day delivered a combination of operational problem-solving and strategic process improvements. Significant progress was made in stabilising the Hermes automation environment, introducing a more robust development management structure within Asana, progressing critical procurement and production activities, and successfully delivering a complex CV extraction and processing task despite system access limitations. The ongoing focus remains on resolving remote access compatibility issues and completing the wider Hermes/OpenClaw architecture review to strengthen long-term system reliability.

data.name: 1263 Cannon St Diagnostic Visit
data.notes:
Check lift before resumption of Service Contract at 108 Cannon Street:
Lift, stairs,
    Test whole lift operation for function ( noted slight judder in motion worst at half way ).  tested OK ( bar the slight judder).
    Checked entrapment reverse feature on the step barrier both, under bar and over the top. operated as designed, good speed. tested OK.
    Platform 4mm low to top landing, two of the steps slightly out of alignment on one side in home position.
PLC, Electrics/Hydraulics.
    PLC. Clean and dry, no signs of either moisture ingress nor oil leaks from the power pack/ valve block. Backup Batteries tested at 13volts each !!!
    Electrical distribution box, clean and dry. connections good/secure.
Scissor lift/ side barrier.
    Stairs forward limit switch currently on a weighted cable., operating OK
    Lift from pit. Left guide roller wheel as viewed from entrance door into pit not touching pit trim. clearance of 2mm approx. ( this maybe accounting for the slight judder when lift is moving.)
    Bottom bearing wheels on scissor have light corrosion as does the lift frame where the wheels run giving a slight pitted surface.
    Side barrier lifting ram has a slight drip or oil from the breather ( top port of ram) which has left residue on fittings and needle valve below making it look like they are leaking !!
Conclusion.
Overall the lift is dusty and a little dirty, operates correctly as does safety features. the guide roller needs adjusting to eliminate the judder. The floor of the pit room immediately below the bottom step is covered in dirt/rubbish from the pavement above.

data.name: Prevent recurrence – Sesame lifting-equipment identification, certification and site-release process
data.notes:
CHARLIE-CREATED PREVENTIVE ACTION

Created by Charlie at Steven’s request on 2 September 2026, following the Manchester Town Hall / Albert Square lifting-equipment stoppage.

Charlie has drafted the process below from the live incident, Sesame’s existing lifting-equipment records and current HSE guidance. It is a proposed company control, not a substitute for the project lifting plan or advice from the competent person carrying out LOLER thorough examinations. Les and Giles must review it, improve anything impractical and give the requested feedback before it is adopted.


Why this task exists

Sesame’s 2,000 kg lifting beam reached site with a thorough-examination record available, but the physical serial number could not be read. Rob Owen, the Appointed Person, could not positively match the beam to its record and would not accept responsibility for its use. The slings did not have readily available matching certification, and the shackle being used was identified as AA88 after a different record had initially been provided.

Rob accepted an immediate workaround only on the basis that Les clearly re-marks the verified beam number while it is on site and that the identification remains clear when the beam returns. New compliant slings and shackles are also being obtained for the present job.

This clears the immediate installation but does not fix the company-wide weakness. Sesame currently has related records spread across several tasks and evidence locations, but no single release-to-site gate proving that every physical beam, gantry, sling, shackle and hoist is legibly identified, in date, certificate-matched and listed correctly in the lifting plan before it leaves.

Incident source: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1198301119883979/f/
Earlier missing-inspection warning: https://app.asana.com/0/0/1215751097716202/f/


Required outcome

Les and Giles are to create, test and implement one practical controlled process covering all Sesame-owned, hired or borrowed lifting equipment and lifting accessories used by Sesame, including gantries, A-frames, lifting and spreader beams, trolleys, chain blocks and hoists, lifting chains, wire and web slings/strops, shackles, hooks, eyebolts and any equipment added later.

The process must make it impossible, so far as reasonably practicable, for unidentified, certificate-mismatched, overdue, damaged or unrecorded lifting equipment to be packed for site use.


Responsibilities

    Les – operational owner: physical inspection, equipment selection against the lifting plan, packing, pre-use checks, release-to-site confirmation, site substitution control and return inspection.
    Giles – asset and evidence owner: master register, purchase records, manufacturer information, Declarations of Conformity where applicable, current Reports of Thorough Examination, expiry controls, arranging examinations/replacements and documentary release confirmation.
    Competent person / examiner: statutory thorough examinations, examination scheme where used, defect decisions and advice on any permanent re-identification method. Les and Giles must not treat their internal checks as a substitute for a thorough examination.



1. Close out the Albert Square equipment correctly

    When the 2,000 kg beam returns, place it in a controlled hold area until the permanent identity check below is completed. The temporary marker applied on site is not, by itself, the permanent fix.
    Using the current report, manufacturer records and existing photographs, verify the exact original serial or unique identifier belonging to that physical beam. Do not copy a number onto it unless the match is positively established.
    Agree a durable, legible and non-damaging permanent identification method. Do not stamp, drill, weld, grind or otherwise alter a load-bearing member unless the manufacturer or competent examiner has confirmed that the method is acceptable.
    Ensure the beam’s SWL is also clearly visible. Photograph the whole beam, the permanent identifier and SWL, then link those photographs to the asset record and matching examination report.
    Add the new slings and shackles obtained for the current job to the register before they are accepted into Sesame stock. Record each item’s own identity, WLL/SWL, evidence and examination status rather than treating a supplier invoice as sufficient proof.
    If the original identity cannot be established reliably, keep the beam quarantined and obtain a decision from the competent person/manufacturer on re-identification and examination before it is released again.



2. Complete a 100% physical lifting-equipment census

Les and Giles are to inspect every workshop item, van kit and equipment set together. For each individual item, or each genuinely controlled matched set, the master register must contain:
    Sesame asset ID and manufacturer serial/unique identifier;
    equipment type, manufacturer, model and useful description;
    SWL/WLL, including any configuration-dependent limits;
    current physical location, van, kit or quarantine area;
    date acquired and Declaration of Conformity/manufacturer evidence where applicable;
    current Report of Thorough Examination, examination date, examiner and next due date or written examination-scheme interval;
    clear photograph of the complete item, identifier and SWL/WLL marking;
    condition and release status: GREEN – available, AMBER – action due before next use, or RED – quarantined / do not use;
    owner and any controlled set or lifting-plan relationship.


Every item must be accounted for. An item not present during the census remains RED until physically inspected and reconciled.


3. Reconcile the physical equipment to the evidence

    Match each physical identifier directly to the correct report and other supporting evidence. Similar description, capacity or appearance is not enough.
    Where an identifier is unreadable, missing or different from the report; the SWL/WLL is unclear; evidence is missing; the examination is overdue; or damage/deterioration is found, attach a RED quarantine tag and physically separate the item from usable stock.
    Arrange competent examination, manufacturer clarification, repair or replacement as appropriate. Do not solve a traceability failure by guessing or simply copying an unverified number.
    Choose and document one authoritative repository for permanent certificate/examination evidence. Asana should show the current status and direct evidence link, not rely on scattered duplicate uploads. Do not delete existing evidence until any migration has been checked and read back successfully.
    Consolidate or cross-link the existing Sesame records below so staff have one master register and do not need to search several incomplete lists.


Existing records to reconcile:
    https://app.asana.com/0/0/1201399182013791/f/
    https://app.asana.com/0/0/1204732963294870/f/
    https://app.asana.com/0/0/1178857188392489/f/
    https://app.asana.com/0/0/1203336812958893/f/
    https://app.asana.com/0/0/1215751097716202/f/



4. Introduce a two-person release-to-site gate

Complete this no later than two working days before planned travel wherever the programme permits. Urgent work still requires the same evidence; urgency must not become an undocumented bypass.

Les – physical and operational release:
    Select the exact equipment required by the approved lifting plan and list its Sesame asset ID and manufacturer serial/identifier.
    Confirm each item is physically present, suitable for the intended load/configuration, undamaged, legibly identified and marked with the applicable SWL/WLL.
    Carry out and record the required pre-use check.
    Confirm that slings, shackles, beams, hoists and gantries have been selected as one compatible system and that the lift plan reflects the actual equipment.


Giles – documentary release:
    Confirm every listed physical identifier matches the current evidence record.
    Confirm the examination is in date and any conditions or next-action dates in the report have been complied with.
    Confirm the complete evidence pack is available to Les and, where required, to the main contractor/Appointed Person before arrival, including an offline copy where site connectivity may be unreliable.
    Confirm hired or newly purchased equipment has been entered and checked to the same standard before release.


Release rule: equipment does not leave until Les and Giles have both recorded GREEN release. If an item fails, replace it with another verified item or hire compliant equipment and update the lifting plan/evidence pack before departure.


5. Control site use and substitutions

    Carry out pre-use checks at the start of use and after any event that may have affected condition.
    Do not substitute a beam, sling, shackle, hoist or gantry on site merely because it has the same capacity. Record the substitute’s exact identity, verify its evidence and update/approve the lifting plan as required before use.
    Report damage, lost tags, illegible markings, overload, shock loading, contamination or unusual events immediately and quarantine affected equipment.
    Keep the evidence pack available for the Appointed Person and site team throughout the lifting operation.



6. Control the return to Sesame

    Les records return date, location and condition for every item or controlled set.
    Clean and inspect the equipment before storage. Repair or replace protective labels before they become unreadable.
    Quarantine any damaged, incomplete, contaminated or unidentified item rather than returning it to usable stock.
    Giles updates the register and arranges any examination, repair or replacement triggered by the return check.



7. Examination and reminder controls

    Record the interval required by the competent person’s written examination scheme where one applies.
    Where no written scheme sets another interval, use the HSE default maximum intervals: six months for lifting accessories and equipment used to lift people, and twelve months for other lifting equipment.
    Set advance reminders early enough to avoid site disruption, provisionally six weeks and two weeks before expiry.
    Carry out a monthly internal visual check of location, label/marking legibility and obvious condition, plus a quarterly physical-to-register reconciliation. These are Sesame preventive controls and do not replace pre-use checks or statutory thorough examination.
    Servicing, maintenance and internal inspection must not be described as a LOLER thorough examination unless it was completed and reported by a suitable competent person.



Completion evidence required

    Albert Square beam identity permanently resolved, photographed and directly matched to its current report, or formally quarantined pending competent-person action;
    new slings and shackles registered and evidence-matched;
    100% census completed, with every unresolved item physically quarantined;
    one master lifting-equipment register agreed and existing records reconciled/cross-linked;
    one authoritative evidence repository agreed and accessible;
    release-to-site and return-check templates created;
    process piloted on the next installation requiring Sesame lifting equipment;
    installation team briefed through a short toolbox talk;
    Les and Giles feedback received separately and final amendments adopted by Steven/management.



Feedback required from Les and Giles

Please each comment separately on this task before it is completed:
    What, if anything, is impractical in the proposed process?
    Which lifting-equipment categories, evidence fields or failure cases have Charlie missed?
    Are the responsibilities between Les, Giles and the competent examiner correct?
    Is the two-working-day release gate workable, and what controlled route should apply to genuine urgent work?
    Do you accept the process, or what exact amendments do you recommend?


Do not mark this task complete until both Les and Giles have responded and the final process has been approved for Sesame use.


Current HSE guidance used by Charlie

    https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/thorough-examinations-lifting-equipment.htm
